head: b3edfa2e5522bee094eca6e694ce867ffd23d987
summary:
Attempt 2 (b3edfa2) changes only .taad/fitness.yaml. Nothing under src/ or tests/ moved, and the worktree yaml equals HEAD. The file is still pure ASCII (7704 bytes, 0 non-ASCII). Both TheScannerCoreDoesNotKnowAboutTheScreen patterns (lines 47 and 57) now read `(?m)^﻿?\s*using…`, with the escape written as six ASCII characters. The header gains the authoring rule for it and a rewritten parity sentence.

I re-diffed every pattern against the ArchitectureRulesTests.cs literals: all 8 entries equal the literal plus `(?m)`, and the two screen patterns also carry the `﻿?` that the m1 decision authorised. The Fitness MCP op=check in the worktree still reports '8 rule(s) checked against 33 file(s) read. Every declared rule holds.'

On the scratch copy with the new yaml, all of these fail at the right place:
- a BOM plus line-1 `using System.Windows;` fails at Scanner.cs:1; attempt 1 passed it, and xUnit fails there too, as measured in attempt 1
- the no-BOM line-1 plant fails at :1
- a BOM plus an indented `using static FsAnalyser.App.X;` fails at :1
- a line-7 plant fails at :6, the declared offset

A BOM file with no violation, and a BOM plus `using System.IO;`, still pass. The engine's _append_rules still leaves the file as an exact prefix and loads 9 rules. git check-ignore still finds no match. O-007 is discharged.

One thing is left, and it is minor. The rewritten header sentence at lines 15-16 now guarantees full parity for any UTF-8 file under 2 MB, and that is measurably false. I planted `// DllImport` in src/FsAnalyser.Core/packages/Planted.cs, a UTF-8 file with no BOM. Fitness passed and read 33 files, so it never opened Planted.cs. xUnit failed InteropLivesOnlyInNative at Planted.cs:1. The cause is that Fitness prunes any directory named packages, dist, target, node_modules and so on (fitness.py:325-327), while xUnit excludes only bin and obj. Line 38 of the header likewise says Fitness prunes only bin/ and obj/. I recorded this as drift in attempt 1; now that the sentence makes an explicit guarantee, it is filed as m1-2. Nothing in the tree triggers it, and xUnit remains the backstop.

findings.claim: The new parity guarantee in the .taad/fitness.yaml header is false for a UTF-8 file under 2 MB that sits under a directory Fitness prunes by name. Lines 15-16 say: 'In a UTF-8 file under 2 MB, with or without a byte-order mark, every violation xUnit reports is also reported here in the same file'. The engine skips every directory named .git, .hg, .svn, node_modules, bin, obj, .vs, .idea, __pycache__, .venv, venv, dist, .next, target or packages, at any depth (taad3/fitness.py:325-327, applied at :408). xUnit's Files() excludes only path parts that equal "bin" or "obj" (ArchitectureRulesTests.cs:78). So a violation in, for example, src/FsAnalyser.Core/packages/X.cs fails xUnit and passes Fitness. The file is never read, and the rule still counts as matched through its other files. Line 38 compounds it by saying Fitness prunes only 'bin/ and obj/ by name'. A second, lesser divergence of the same direction, found by reading the code and not measured: xUnit's reparse-rule exemptions use `.Except([...])`, which is case-sensitive (ArchitectureRulesTests.cs:31), while Fitness's except_files globs are compiled with re.I (fitness.py:216). A case-only rename of EntryClassifier.cs or Kernel32.cs would therefore fail xUnit and pass Fitness. This is the same claim class as m1, whose decision required the sentence to be made true. Nothing in the current tree triggers it, and xUnit remains the backstop.
findings.evidence: Measured in %TEMP%\sl022-review\tree (a copy of the tracked files plus the attempt-2 yaml). I created src/FsAnalyser.Core/packages/Planted.cs as UTF-8 with no BOM, 2 lines, first line `// DllImport planted in a directory named packages`. Engine fitness.check: verdict pass, content_files=33 (unchanged, so Planted.cs was not read), unmatched=[]. `dotnet test --no-build --filter ArchitectureRulesTests` on the same tree: InteropLivesOnlyInNative [FAIL] with `src\FsAnalyser.Core\packages\Planted.cs:1: /(Library|Dll)Import/`.
findings.fix: In the KNOWN DIVERGENCES paragraph (lines 17-21), add: 'and a file under a directory Fitness skips by name (packages, dist, target, node_modules, venv/.venv, .vs, .idea, .next, __pycache__, .git; xUnit skips only bin and obj)'. Change line 38's '(it prunes bin/ and obj/ by name)' to '(it prunes only a fixed list of directory names, such as bin/, obj/ and packages/)'. No pattern change is needed. The engine-side fix, pruning by .gitignore rather than by name, is outside this repo.

.taad/fitness.yaml:47 and :57 read `'(?m)^﻿?\s*using\s+(static\s+)?(System\.Windows|PresentationFramework|FsAnalyser\.App)'` as ASCII escapes (0 non-ASCII bytes). The header's authoring rule is at lines 28-31, and lines 15-21 name UTF-16/UTF-32 and files over 2 MB as divergences. Scratch plants against this yaml:
- BOM plus a line-1 `using System.Windows;` in Scanner.cs fails at :1; the attempt-1 yaml passed it, and xUnit failed at :1 in my attempt-1 run.
- The no-BOM line-1 plant fails at :1.

- The BOM-only clean file and BOM plus `using System.IO;` both pass.
The rewritten sentence is still incomplete; see m2.

cases.evidence: The worktree yaml loads under the Fitness MCP op=check (8 rules), and patterns containing \b, \s and now ﻿ are single-quoted and ASCII-only.
`git check-ignore -v -n --no-index .taad/fitness.yaml` finds no match, and the file is tracked at b3edfa2.
Scratch plants against the attempt-2 yaml: line-7 `using System.Windows;` in Scanner.cs fails at :6 (the declared offset). Line-1 plants with and without a BOM fail at :1.
Unchanged entries. The attempt-1 scratch plant `/* DllImport */` failed InteropLivesOnlyInNative (src). The yaml diff does not touch these entries.
The csproj entry's pattern changed only by `﻿?`. The attempt-1 UseWPF-in-Core.csproj plant hit a different, unchanged pattern. The xaml entry is unchanged.
The reparse entries are unchanged by the diff. The attempt-1 plants in MainWindow.xaml.cs failed at :317.
The clean tree passes (MCP op=check) with Kernel32.cs and EntryClassifier.cs holding the tokens. except_files are unchanged.
MCP op=check passes over ArchitectureRulesTests.cs with including_comments: true.
MCP op=check shows no MATCHED NO FILES. The globs are unchanged.
The worktree op=check ran with .dotnet/ and obj/ present and read 33 files, the same as the clean scratch copy. A directory named packages/ nested inside a rooted scope is also pruned; see m2.
A declared no-op, and the reason still holds: no pattern in the attempt-2 yaml contains `$`.
The never-skipped entry is unchanged. The attempt-1 plants (Skip=, Explicit=true, two-line Skip) fail it.
Non-material per the design, and still nothing to build.
Re-run of _append_rules on the attempt-2 yaml: 9 rules, original bytes an exact prefix.

drift: The two screen-rule patterns are no longer the xUnit literal plus `(?m)` only: they add `﻿?` after ^. That goes beyond the design's allowed transforms (leading (?m), quote escaping, inline flags, \r? before $). The m1 decision authorised it and the yaml header declares it (lines 28-31), but the build's 'departures' list names only the csproj glob, and O-001's recorded discharge text ('each equal to the literal plus a leading (?m)') no longer describes the tree exactly.
The declared csproj-glob departure (`src/FsAnalyser.Core/**/*.csproj`) is unchanged and still correct.

Header line 14 still describes the offset as 'a (?m)^\s* match' while the pattern is now `(?m)^﻿?\s*`. The behaviour it describes (reported at the first preceding blank line) is unchanged, as measured: the line-7 plant is reported at :6.
